requirements.requirement: Concurrent successful exports use private, non-colliding temporary storage and retain all invoice rows.
requirements.summary: The installed script creates a unique temporary directory beside each destination under umask 077. Forty concurrent exports completed without failures; all 40 outputs matched the three-line source, and no temporary directories remained.

requirements.requirement: Pre-existing symlinks cannot redirect export writes, and the protected sentinel remains intact.
requirements.summary: The prepared hostile tmp/export.tmp symlink remained present and unfollowed. A symlink supplied as the output pathname was replaced by a regular export without modifying its protected target; the sentinel hash continued to match the preparation baseline, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: An export failure leaves the prior destination intact.
requirements.summary: A forced final-rename failure returned nonzero while the existing destination retained its original content and hash.

requirements.requirement: Temporary export files are removed when the utility exits.
requirements.summary: Successful single, concurrent, symlink-defense, and post-restart runs reported zero leftover temporary directories. The forced failure also left none; the installed script includes exit and signal cleanup traps.
Both files retained the hashes, sizes, ownership, and modes recorded before the repair, including after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software.
requirements.summary: The node remained Ubuntu 16.04.7 with kernel 4.4.0-210-generic before and after the work. The repaired utility is a POSIX shell script using commands demonstrably available on that platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The repaired exporter produced complete concurrent outputs, resisted both the seeded temporary-file symlink and an output-path symlink, preserved existing destinations on failure, cleaned temporary storage, and preserved protected data and the legacy platform. The mandatory restart protocol is strong: it records a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement and connection interruption, a different post-restart boot ID, and recovered system, utility, data, and security behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Temporary-directory privacy was established from the captured installed implementation (umask 077 plus mktemp -d) rather than an in-flight permission inspection.
Cleanup was behaviorally tested on normal success and a forced failure; signal-triggered cleanup was supported by the captured traps but not directly exercised.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. The persistent bin/export replacement directly implemented the repair. Test directories, files, and symlinks were bounded evidence fixtures and were cleaned; the directory accidentally left by the failed symlink-test setup was explicitly removed by the next command. The initial unprivileged installation attempt failed at redirection with no evidence of a state change. The reboot was required by the provider-wide protocol, and repeated failed polls were read-only availability checks. Final lifecycle evidence shows no failed services, package damage, listening-socket exposure, or executor test residue.
